contexts.text: Scientific things, regarded in themselves, are donkeys and men-servants; their pleasures of those things, are maidservants and she-donkeys. ().
Horses, mules, and donkeys, when mentioned in the Word = intellectual, rational, and scientific things.
By men-servants and maidservants, young men, and donkeys, by means of whom he will do his work () are signified rational and scientific things, by which he will confirm (falsities).
(Abraham) saddled the donkey = the natural man whom he prepared.
By a camel is signified what is scientific in general; and by a donkey, what is scientific in particular.

There are two things which constitute the Natural with man... namely, natural good and natural truth; natural good is the delight flowing forth from charity and faith; natural truth is the Scientific of them. That natural truth is what is signified by a donkey, Illustrated.
Young donkeys () = scientific things in particular.
Sending the foot of the ox and of the donkey () = natural things that are of service. The ox = the Natural as to good; the donkey, the Natural as to truth.

Binding his donkey's colt unto the vine, and the son of his she-donkey to the noble vine (). Donkey's colt = natural truth; son of a she-donkey = rational truth. The reason the son of a she-donkey = rational truth, is because a she-donkey = the affection of natural truth, the son of which is rational truth.
A Judge formerly rode upon a she-donkey, and his sons upon donkey's colts; the reason being that Judges represented the goods of the Church, and their sons, truths thence derived. Illustrated.

A she-donkey represented and signified the affection of natural good and truth; a she-mule, the affection of rational truth; a donkey, or donkey's colt, natural truth itself; and a mule, and also the son of a she-donkey, rational truth. Illustrated.
To ride upon a donkey () was a sign that the Natural was subordinated; and to ride upon a foal the son of a she-donkey, that the Rational was subordinated.
As by an ox, and a donkey is signified the natural man as to good and truth, there were many laws given, in which oxen and donkeys are mentioned. Illustrated.
To carry their wealth on the shoulder of young donkeys () = the knowledges which are in their Rational. A young donkey = rational truth.
A chariot of a donkey () = a mass of particular scientifics.
Camels, donkeys, etc. () = truths in special.

And camels and donkeys () = the exterior and external truths of good. Camels = general scientific things of the natural man. General scientific things are lower, or exterior, truths of good. And donkeys = truths of natural good still lower, or external. AC 4038:end. AC 4244.
Twenty she-donkeys and ten foals, etc. () = things that serve, general and special. She-donkeys and their foals = those things which are of the natural man.
And their donkeys () = truths thence derived; namely, from natural and rational good.
In his feeding the donkeys of Zibeon his father () = when he was in scientifics.
They laded their provisions upon their donkeys () = truths collected together into scientific things... A donkey = what is scientific.

These words are spiritually apprehended when the correspondences are understood in place of them; namely... scientific things which are in the Natural instead of donkeys. That by donkeys, in the Word, are signified things that serve; thus scientific things...
To give fodder to his donkey in the inn = when they reflected about the scientific things in the exterior Natural... Donkey = scientific things.

To take us for slaves, and our donkeys = that whatever is in each Natural is of no account... Donkeys = those things which are in the Natural, which are scientific things; here, in the exterior Natural; because the truths which are signified by the sons of Jacob, are in the interior Natural.

He gave fodder for their donkeys = instruction concerning good. By donkeys are signified scientific things. Hence by giving fodder to the donkeys is signified instruction concerning the good of scientific things.
The men were sent away, they and their donkeys = that the outward natural man was somewhat removed, with its truths and scientific things... Donkeys = scientific things.

As to the signification of donkeys, it is to be known, that they have one signification when they served for riding on; for upon donkeys, she-donkeys, and mules rode the Judges, the Kings, and their sons, and they then signified rational, and also natural truth and good. Hence it was that the Lord, as a Judge, and also as a King, when He entered Jerusalem, rode upon a she-donkey with a foal: for this was a sign of the judicial function, and also of the kingly one. But donkeys had another signification when they served for carrying a burden, as here. They then signified scientific things... AE 31:7.
Everyone laded upon his donkey, and returned to the city = that truths were brought back from sensual things into scientific things. A donkey = what is scientific.

It was forbidden to plough with an ox and a donkey together (), because to plough with an ox = good in the Natural, and to plough with a donkey = truth there. A donkey = scientific truth, thus truth in the Natural. The interior or spiritual cause of this command was, that the Angels could not bear to have a separate idea of good and truth... AC 7601:8. AC 10184:6. AC 10669:5.
Ten donkeys carrying of the good of Egypt = scientific things with many things that serve... Donkeys = scientific things.
And ten she-donkeys carrying corn and bread = the truth of good and the good of truth... She-donkeys = things that serve.

The reason she-donkeys bore the corn and bread, and donkeys, the good of Egypt, is that by donkeys are signified things which serve in so far as they have reference to truth, and by she-donkeys are signified things which serve in so far as they have reference to good.
Donkeys = things that serve.
He binds his donkey's colt to the vine = truth in the Natural for the outward Church... A donkey = truth in the Natural. AE 433:4.
And the son of his she-donkey to the excellent vine = truth from the Rational for the inward Church... The son of a she-donkey = rational truth. AE 433:4.
A bony donkey = the lowest service. A donkey = service. Explained. AE 445:4.
The works that flow from the affection of love (towards self) are like the burdens which the lower sort of donkeys carry.
Moses made (his wife and sons) ride upon a donkey = those things which might serve the new intelligence... A donkey = truth serving; here, of new intelligence.
Into the horses, into the donkeys, into the camels () = intellectual and scientific things of the truth that is of faith... Donkeys = things that serve the Intellectual, thus also scientific things.

Every opening of a donkey thou shalt redeem in small cattle = that faith merely natural must not be ascribed to the Lord, but the truth of innocence which is therein... A donkey = what is natural, for by a donkey is signified what is scientific, also what serves, and thus also the Natural, for scientific things are of the Natural, and the Natural, relatively to the Spiritual, is what serves.
Donkey (in the tenth commandment) = the affection of natural truth. TCR 325. AE 1022:2.
And an ox or a donkey hath fallen therein = that it has perverted good or truth in the Natural... A donkey = truth in the Natural. References. AC 9088.
From an ox even to a donkey () = from good or truth exterior... A donkey = the truth of the Natural.
When thou meetest the ox of thine enemy, or his donkey, going astray = good not genuine, and truth not genuine, with those who are out of the Church... A donkey = the truth of the outward man.

When thou shalt see the donkey of him that hateth thee lying under its burden = falsity not agreeing with the good of the Church, from which it is about to perish... A donkey = scientific truth; thus, in the opposite sense, scientific falsity.
To send forth the foot of the ox and of the donkey = to be instructed in outward goods and truths.
That thine ox and thine donkey may rest = the tranquillity of peace for outward goods and truths together... Donkey = outward truth.
A donkey = the Natural, because it = what serves. Hence a millstone turned by a donkey () = a natural and worldly Scientific. AE 1182:3.
A donkey () = science. References.
Afar off they appear like donkeys carrying burdens. TCR 333:end.
One seen sitting on a glowing donkey...
(The speaking of Balaam's donkey, Explained.)

I will here explain... the arcanum about the she-donkey on which Balaam rode... As Balaam rode on the she-donkey, he continually meditated his sorceries against the Sons of Israel... By the she-donkey on which he rode, in the spiritual sense of the Word, is signified an enlightened Intellectual; wherefore to ride upon a she-donkey, or she-mule, was an ensign of a Chief Judge, or of a King... Hence by the she-donkey turning three times out of the way, is signified that an enlightened understanding does not agree with the thought of a sorcerer... It sounded to Balaam as if the she-donkey had spoken to him, but still she did not speak; yet still the speech was heard as if from her. From experience.
White she-donkeys () = the Rational as to good.
Which of you shall have a donkey or an ox fallen into a pit (). By a donkey and an ox are signified the truth and good of the natural man...
Donkeys () = the things of the sensual man.
The flesh of donkeys () = man's Own Voluntary.
(The donkey included among animals of an intermediate character which appear in the world of Spirits.)
